thread:
Samir: quick question — rolling a tiny change to /v1/generate to include a top-level `schema_version` and to make `metadata` optional. opinions on omitted vs null for optional nested fields?
Jia: prefer omitted when unknown. null tends to break some mobile clients that expect a map.
Tanvi: +1 omitted for compatibility. Also we should explicitly document when we intentionally return `null` (eg: field exists but value unknown).
Luis: one caveat: analytics wants consistent keys for downstream tooling. If we omit, pipelines have to tolerate missing keys. If we null, they can rely on the key presence. tradeoffs.
Samir: good point. proposal: default to omitted, but add `X-Redwood-Schema: v2` header so consumers can opt-in to "strict" mode where keys are always present (possibly null).
Jia: that would work. we can do header + contract doc. also support `Accept: application/x-ndjson` for streaming, but schema header should still apply to each ndjson event.
Tanvi: example headers we should publish in the docs snippet:
```
Content-Type: application/json
X-Redwood-Schema: v2
Accept: application/json
```
and for streaming:
```
Content-Type: application/x-ndjson
X-Redwood-Schema: v2
Accept: application/x-ndjson
```
Samir: yep. for the JSON body example i'm thinking something like:
```
{
  "schema_version": "2",
  "result": {"text":"..."},
  "metadata": {"source":"rlhf"} // optional, can be omitted
}
```
Luis: maybe call out that `metadata` is recommended to be an object when present; if we return null in strict mode, it should be `null` not "null".
Jia: can we add a migration note: older clients (pre-v2) will ignore the `schema_version` header and continue. server should still accept requests without the header.
Samir: yes — backwards compatibility rule: server defaults to "lenient" (omitted-allowed) unless `X-Redwood-Schema: v2` is set. No breaking changes for existing users.
Tanvi: i'll draft the contract PR. question: does anyone object to using `schema_version` as a top-level field in the body vs only in a header?
Luis: i prefer header for routing and observability, but body is helpful for proxies that strip headers. both is fine; prefer header as source of truth.
Jia: agree. header primary, body field optional mirror.
Samir: ok will capture both in the RFC: header-required-for-strict, body-`schema_version` optional mirror. also add an explicit line about "missing vs null" semantics and how SDKs should surface it (sdk: treat missing as undefined, null as explicit None).
ci-bot: deploy pipeline passed for branch `feature/schema-v2` :white_check_mark:
Samir: awesome. @Tanvi please ping when PR is up, i'll add the tests for ndjson streaming + header enforcement.
Tanvi: will do, aiming for EOD. thanks all :rocket:
